what_its_for: Terconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat vaginal yeast infections (also called vaginal candidiasis). It works by stopping the growth of the fungus that causes the infection, helping to relieve itching, burning, and discharge.
how_to_take: Terconazole comes as a vaginal cream or suppository (ovule) that you insert directly into your vagina. Wash your hands well before and after use. Use the applicator provided to insert the cream, or unwrap the suppository and insert it as directed. Lie down after inserting to help keep the medicine in place. Use this medicine at bedtime for best results. Use the full course of treatment even if your symptoms improve before you finish, and even if your period starts during treatment.
dosing: Follow your doctor's instructions exactly. The usual treatment is: 0.4% cream used once nightly for 7 nights, OR 0.8% cream used once nightly for 3 nights, OR 80 mg suppository inserted once nightly for 3 nights. Do not use more than prescribed or skip doses.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not use two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Try to use the medicine at the same time each night.
storage: Store terconazole at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the cream tube tightly closed. Do not freeze the cream or suppositories. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Throw away any unused medicine after your treatment is complete.
what_to_avoid: Avoid sexual intercourse while using this medicine, as it may cause discomfort and the medicine could affect your partner. Do not use tampons, douches, or other vaginal products during treatment unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Be aware that terconazole can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms, making them less effective — consider using another form of birth control during treatment and for 3 days after finishing. Avoid getting the medicine in your eyes.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe vaginal burning, itching, or irritation that is new or gets worse; rash, hives, or skin redness anywhere on your body; swelling of the face, lips, or throat; fever, chills, or stomach pain; foul-smelling discharge; or if your symptoms do not improve within 3 days or do not go away completely within 7 days of finishing treatment. Also call your doctor if you are not sure you have a yeast infection — this medicine does not treat bacterial infections.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some relief from itching and burning within 1 to 3 days of starting treatment. However, it is very important to finish the entire prescribed course of treatment even if you feel better. Full relief usually occurs within a few days after completing treatment. If your symptoms have not improved after 3 days or have not completely cleared up after finishing all doses, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant before using this medicine. It is generally avoided in the first trimester; use in the second and third trimester only if clearly needed and directed by your doctor. Breastfeeding: It is not known if terconazole passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using if you are breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is not recommended for girls who have not yet had their first menstrual period. Always check with a doctor before using in young patients. Allergies: Tell your doctor if you have had an allergic reaction to terconazole or other antifungal medicines in the past.
